title: Hold 'til Dawn match worker control v1
description: The directory listens on IPv4 loopback. Each worker connects and retains ENet and simulation ownership across TCP sessions.
$comment: The schema validates a decoded JSON envelope. x-protocol specifies framing and payload contracts: managerCommands keys are every frame the manager may send and workerEvents keys are every frame a worker may send; each entry references its payload contract in $defs.

cancel.description: The manager sends {requestId}. The worker resolves a requestId through its request ledger and also accepts a direct {ticketId}.

heartbeat.description: The state projection plus the heartbeat bookkeeping fields.

requestId.description: Echoed from the reserve request. Empty only when the request requestId was not a valid token, which pairs with code invalid_request.

launch.slotMarker: The manager appends --htd-slot=<udpPort>-<generation> as the worker's final command-line argument, and an optional --path <project directory> may precede -- when the worker is launched outside the server directory. Both the local process scan and the systemd /proc/<pid>/cmdline check identify the owning process by matching this exact final argument, so the marker must stay last. The worker dispatches on --match-worker only and ignores the marker value.

environment.MATCH_GENERATION: Opaque unique generation token assigned before spawn.
environment.MATCH_ROOM_NAME: Initial creator name, stripped and truncated to 16 characters.
environment.ADMISSION_SECRET_FILE: Protected file readable by the manager and worker containing 32 bytes as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, optionally followed by a newline.

launch.readiness: A bound UDP socket is not readiness. Wait for signed ready. The worker exits nonzero on invalid initial configuration, bind failure, failed control authentication, or a 5 second initial control deadline.

x-protocol.framing: 4-byte unsigned big-endian byte length, then 1 to 8192 UTF-8 bytes containing the JSON envelope. Close the TCP session on malformed frame, invalid MAC, wrong context, unexpected counter, or handshake error.
x-protocol.envelopeSigning: HMAC-SHA-256 over UTF-8 lines hold-til-dawn/control, version, direction, roomId, generation, udpPort, counter, type, body, joined by LF with no final LF. body is canonical padded RFC 4648 Base64 of UTF-8 JSON object bytes as sent. Sign the encoded body bytes unchanged. mac is lowercase hexadecimal. Counters are canonical decimal strings and must increase by exactly one in each direction.
registration: Worker hello (counter 1, host recovery key) with {pid, nonce, reportSequence}. nonce is 32 fresh random bytes in lowercase hex. reportSequence is the last emitted heartbeat sequence, initially 0.

Manager challenge (counter 1, host recovery key) with {workerNonce, managerNonce}. Echo hello.nonce; managerNonce is 32 fresh random bytes in lowercase hex. Verify against the expected room, generation, UDP port and process lease before replying.

Both derive the session key as HMAC-SHA-256 with the raw host recovery key over UTF-8 lines hold-til-dawn/session, 1, roomId, generation, udpPort, pid, reportSequence, workerNonce, managerNonce with no final LF. Use raw digest bytes as the new key. pid and reportSequence use decimal.
Worker register (counter 2, session key) with {pid, reportSequence}. Manager registered (counter 2, session key) with {}. Both must verify the derived key before processing later records.

Worker ready with a state projection, then heartbeat with state, sequence and maxFrameMs. Retain the last observed sequence for the generation when reconciling duplicate or stale publishers. Restarted managers reconstruct from authenticated state and retain port leases until process ownership is reconciled.

After initial readiness the worker reconnects every 250 ms after control loss, with fresh nonces and counters. The manager answers each heartbeat with signed ping, which keeps at least one signed response per second flowing. Each side enforces its own authenticated-traffic deadline: the worker drops its control session after 5000 ms without authenticated inbound traffic, while the manager destroys a control socket idle for 2800 ms and treats a slot as offline until an authenticated state report arrives within 2800 ms of the last. The worker survives control loss. New reservations and ENet admission are suspended until authenticated again, and outstanding tickets continue expiring.

challenge.description: Registration step 2. Sent at counter 1 with the host recovery key, after the hello's room, generation, UDP port and process lease all match expectations.

registered.description: Registration step 4. Sent at counter 2 with the session key and an empty payload, confirming the derived session key.

reserve.description: requestId must be unique for a new operation, scoped to caller and operation by the manager. Retry the identical payload with its original expiresAt. expiresAt is Unix milliseconds, strictly in the future and at most 30000 ms from the worker clock. Ticket lifetime then uses the monotonic worker clock.

cancel.description: The manager sends {requestId} and the worker resolves it through its request ledger; the worker also accepts a direct {ticketId}. A cancel releases a pending ticket only.

ping.description: Empty payload. Sent in reply to each heartbeat; the worker applies no state on receipt.

close.description: Empty payload. Graceful intentional room shutdown. Only send after authenticating the current generation.

hello.description: Registration step 1. Sent at counter 1 with the host recovery key.

register.description: Registration step 3. Sent at counter 2 with the session key, echoing the hello pid and reportSequence.

heartbeat.description: Emitted as the state projection changes and at least every 1000 ms while online. maxFrameMs is the longest observed gap between control polls. available counts physical slots including held vacancies. Only expose it for joining when waiting and creatorAdmitted is true.

creator_admitted.description: A re-registering worker can report creatorAdmitted=true after the event was lost.

reservation.description: Every reply carries the requestId and a reservation code; reserved adds ticketId, secret, expiresAt and ttlMs, the remaining ticket lifetime in monotonic milliseconds, which the manager requires and bounds by its ticket TTL. secret is 32 random bytes encoded as lowercase hexadecimal. Handle room_started as a terminal response including for an already delivered reservation. Do not expose or log credentials except the direct Phase 3 WSS response to their intended client.

reservation_cancelled.description: Sent when the room starts and every outstanding reservation is invalidated; reason is always room_started. The manager resolves the pending operation with room_started.

cancellation.description: Confirms a released ticket with code cancelled, or unknown_ticket when nothing matched. ticketId is empty when the cancel named no known ticket. The manager takes no state from this reply and does not wait for it.

closing.description: Payload {code: closed}. A port can be released after the worker process actually exits.

error.description: Sent for an unknown command type. The manager treats an error frame as a protocol violation and drops the socket; only the worker is expected to recover, by reconnecting.

enetAdmission.versionPolicy: The admission content string identifies the client build, including map compatibility and the format of admitted gameplay payloads. Bump the protocol on incompatible changes to the admission exchange.
procedure: After connecting, c_admission_begin(protocol, content, ticketId, clientNonce). ticketId is 16 bytes and clientNonce is 32 fresh random bytes, both lowercase hex. One challenge attempt per ENet connection.

The worker responds s_admission_challenge(roomId, generation, challenge) or s_admission_result(code). Match roomId and generation against the WSS assignment before proving. challenge is 32 random bytes in lowercase hex.

c_admission_prove(proof) sends lowercase hex HMAC-SHA-256 using raw ticket secret bytes over UTF-8 lines version, roomId, generation, ticketId, decimal ENet peer ID, clientNonce, challenge, joined by LF with no final LF. Neither admission RPC carries the secret.

The worker sends s_admission_result(admitted) after inserting the player. Failure codes are invalid_attempt, incompatible_content, room_unavailable, invalid_ticket, unavailable, invalid_proof, insertion_failed.

A connection has 5000 ms to admit; a challenge has at most 3000 ms within that deadline. There are 13 ENet transport slots to serve up to five humans and bound unadmitted connections. In active play and technical timeouts continue sending c_input on the existing 20 Hz cadence for liveness.
enetAdmission.actions: c_action continues to carry (kind, arg). Ready uses (ready, bool); technical timeout votes use (timeout_vote, [step, bool]) where step is continue or bot and true selects Continue or Bot. A vote can change until its stage closes. The admitted s_snap envelope carries snapshot (Godot Variant bytes compressed with FastLZ) and size (uncompressed byte length). The decoded dictionary includes seed, result, storage and room. room contains name, state, ready and bots (peer-ID arrays), timeout, remainingMs, vacancies (names), votes (affirmative), votesCast, noEngineer and inputAcks (highest received input sequence by admitted peer, including while frozen). Clients continue sending c_input while admitted and use the transport acknowledgement independently of the simulated movement acknowledgement in ps. Resume increments the teleport serial to reject inputs sampled before the pause.
